headline: Energy Leads, Homebuilders Lag as Friday's Breadth Points to a Cautious August Open
body_html:
Friday's session closed out July on a modestly constructive note, with 273 issues advancing against 246 declining across the 519-name universe — a slim but positive tilt. Energy led all sectors with a gain of 1.63%, followed by Software at 0.89% and Industrials at 0.71%. Homebuilders were the day's clear laggard, dropping 1.72%, while Healthcare shed 0.97% and Consumer names gave back 0.89% as the month's final hours unwound.

Single-stock action was dramatic at both ends of the tape. DexCom surged 11.95% and SPS Commerce climbed 11.48%, with SPX Technologies and Eaton adding more than 7% each on the industrial side. The decliners column told a harsher story: Roblox cratered 26.85%, Veracyte lost 22.52%, MasTec fell nearly 19%, and GoDaddy shed 16.7% — moves that reflect earnings-driven re-ratings rather than broad macro pressure.

Heading into the new week, traders will be watching the dollar, which just logged its worst stretch in more than three months amid renewed doubts over Federal Reserve policy. The S&P 500 remains pinned near a contested technical level, and the calendar brings fresh inflation signals from overseas alongside a continued flood of corporate earnings that will test whether July's leadership can hold into August.

briefs.headline: Dollar Posts Worst Weekly Stretch in Over Three Months
briefs.body: The greenback ended July under significant pressure, recording its steepest weekly decline in more than three months as market participants questioned the Federal Reserve's near-term path. Currency weakness of this magnitude typically ripples into commodity prices and multinational earnings expectations — two themes likely to dominate early-week trading desks.

briefs.headline: AI Security Alarm Raised After OpenAI Platform Breach
briefs.body: A confirmed intrusion into OpenAI's Hugging Face infrastructure has validated warnings that have circulated inside the AI industry for months, with one security observer noting that a threshold has effectively been crossed. The episode sharpens regulatory and enterprise scrutiny of AI platform vulnerabilities heading into a week heavy with technology commentary.

briefs.headline: Databricks Pre-IPO Access Offered Through Fintech Broker
briefs.body: Fintech brokerage Clear Street is giving select investors an early entry point into Databricks, the AI-infrastructure firm valued in the vicinity of $188 billion, ahead of a widely anticipated public listing. The move underscores the intensifying appetite for private AI exposure as public-market valuations in the sector remain elevated.

briefs.headline: Data Centre Expansion Drives Demand for Workforce Housing
briefs.body: The infrastructure buildout supporting AI computing capacity is creating a secondary economic effect: a measurable uptick in demand for workforce and affordable housing near major data centre campuses. The trend adds an unexpected dimension to the Homebuilders sector's outlook even as the group was the hardest-hit sector in Friday's session, falling 1.72%.

briefs.headline: Bloomberg Delays Inclusion of Indian Bonds in Global Index
briefs.body: Bloomberg has pushed back the timeline for adding Indian sovereign debt to its flagship global bond index, a decision that complicates New Delhi's efforts to attract foreign fixed-income capital. The delay arrives as Indian companies simultaneously signal intentions to raise consumer prices further, presenting a nuanced inflation picture for emerging-market watchers this week.

briefs.headline: Amazon Chief Addresses Scale of AI Capital Commitments
briefs.body: Amazon's chief executive moved to reassure investors concerned about the company's aggressive artificial-intelligence spending, offering a framework for how returns on that investment are expected to materialise. His remarks helped steady sentiment around large-cap technology capital allocation — a debate that will persist as more hyperscalers report results in the coming days.
